The French government was in crisis talks on Sunday after one of the most violent days of unrest in years left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted and…

posts.text: If you’re just catching up on the demonstrations across Europe which turned violent on Saturday, this is why some of them are happening. Why are people taking to the streets across Europe? People have been protesting in countries across Europe, including Spain, France and Portugal over their unhappiness at the state…

posts.title: Trump says "France is burning" as he blames violence on immigration
posts.text: The US president Donald Trump said “France is burning” and the country has been “shattered” by immigration in a post on Truth Social. He said: “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once-great country. Close your borders…

Elsewhere in Europe, violent protests are also continuing Albania, where thousands have been calling for the prime minister to step down as they rally against poor university conditions, high tuition fees and corruption. Albanian’s capital saw protests on Sunday for a sixth day in a row as the prime minister, Edi…

posts.text: French President Emmanuel Macron will hold a crisis meeting with ministers on Sunday before he addresses the public, Agence France Presse reports. Macron will sit down with members of his cabinet on Sunday, the Elysee has said, ahead of his televised speech to the French public this evening. It was to come as France…

posts.title: Emmanuel Macron to address French public
posts.text: Emmanuel Macron will give a televised address to the French public this evening on the protests and unrest on Saturday. The French President will speak at 8pm French time (6pm GMT), after more than 1,800 people were arrested on Saturday in connection with violence that spread from protests against the cost of living.

Paris police said about 110,000 people took part in a protest march on Saturday against the cost of living and school conditions. Numbers have differed for those nationwide, with authorities saying it was about 550,000 but organisers claiming it was higher at about 800,000. One person died of a heart attack, Paris…

Protests in France caused damage worth hundreds of millions of euros, according to the head of a trade body representing shop owners. About 1,500 shops and retailers were damaged in the demonstrations according to Alexandre Bompard, president of the Retail and Trade Federation. He told LCI television the cost to the…

posts.title: Arrests rise to 1,800 in France
posts.text: More than 1,800 people have been arrested in France over protests on Saturday, the country’s interior minister Laurent Nunez has said. Nunez, in a post on X, said “the Republic will not yield” as more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters have been injured in the demonstrations. “The material damage is…

It’s important to note that protests have also been taking place across Europe. In Italy rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property on fire in central Milan on Saturday. The demonstration escalated after a march against wars and rising living costs began peacefully. However masked protesters threw…

Here’s a selection of photographs from the protests on Saturday and their aftermath, including the City Hall in Limoges. The prefect on Sunday said the blaze in the 143-year-old building had been contained.
